top_story: A US strike campaign launched on 10 June after a helicopter shootdown triggered Iranian retaliation, and by 11 June the exchange had spread from attacks inside Iran to the Gulf of Oman and US-linked military sites in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, putting a fragile ceasefire close to collapse despite Trump briefly halting a planned third night of strikes. This widening geography shows both sides testing coercive pressure while avoiding a clean break into full-scale war, leaving Gulf states exposed as operational battlegrounds and civilian anxiety rising across the region. Alongside that interstate escalation, Israeli force remained lethal on multiple fronts, with a drone strike killing two people in Sidon on 10 June and the killing of a seven-month-old child in the occupied West Bank underscoring how civilians continue to absorb the cost of overlapping conflicts. The regional picture is one of simultaneous military signaling and social trauma, where even tentative de-escalation efforts are being overtaken by violence that is broadening geographically and deepening public insecurity.
